nodes.title: The cohomological weight dictionary
nodes.statement: Write M=M_µ, W_M for its Weyl group, w0M for its longest element and MW for minimal representatives of W_M\W. Let Φ+ have noncompact roots in g/p_std and compact roots in Lie(M); ρ is half their sum and ρ_nc half the noncompact sum. Put d=dim Sh, ℓ+(w)=ℓ(w), ℓ−(w)=d−ℓ(w), Cκ+={w∈MW: −w⁻¹w0M(κ+ρ) is G-dominant}, and Cκ−={w: w⁻¹(κ+ρ) is G-dominant}. Set ν_w(κ)=−w⁻¹w0M(κ+ρ)−ρ, κ_w(ν)=−w0M w(ν+ρ)−ρ, and κ∨=−w0Mκ−2ρ_nc. These are algebraic lattice formulas; no action of absolute W on arbitrary analytic characters of Tʳ(Z_p) is asserted. Extend the supplied Siegel chamber dictionary to these abelian-type data, and prove Vκ^∨⊗ω_Sh = V_(−w0Mκ−2ρ_nc)(−D) on the smooth toroidal compactification; here the canonical line has weight −2ρ_nc and the boundary is reduced.
hypotheses: (G,X) is an abelian-type Shimura datum; G over Q_p is quasi-split. Fix B,T over Q_p and a finite extension F/Q_p splitting G and defining µ, P_µ and the coefficient representations.

Fix neat tame level K^p, compatible smooth admissible toroidal fans and sufficiently deep Iwahori-decomposed K_{p,m,b}, m≥b≥0 and m>0. All coefficient fields contain the required finite characters and cyclotomic extension for torsor reduction.

Coefficients factor through the supplied rank quotient Gʳ=G/Zᵣ(G) and its torus Tʳ. Identify Tʳ with T^c only under the supplied CM-split-centre comparison, retaining its quotient map. Finite slope is the union of finite nonzero-eigenvalue slope windows.
proofSteps: Import the root datum and highest-weight labels, retaining the left-coset convention.
Check the inverse formulas by cancelling w and w0M; restrict algebraic weights to the actual quotient torus.
Compute the determinant of the cotangent representation from the noncompact roots, then use the logarithmic canonical extension and the reduced boundary divisor.

nodes.statement: For separated finite-type ℤ-schemes X construct D(O_X,■) with the fully faithful discrete quasi-coherent derived subcategory, derived pullback and tensor, proper pushforward with its exceptional right adjoint, and open j_! and j_* with restriction. For a smooth structure map q:X→Spec A of pure relative dimension d identify q!A with Ω^d_(X/A)[d]. Include A=ℤ/p^s and its finite flat extensions, with A-flat coherent coefficients. nodes.title: Dynamical compactifications
nodes.statement: A dynamical compactification consists of proper Xbar,Cbar over S, two maps p1,p2, closed subschemes D+,D− with X=Xbar\(D+∪D−) and C=Cbar\(p1*D+∪p2*D−), and p2*D+⊂p1*D+, p1*D−⊂p2*D− on underlying sets. For ideals I,I′ write D≤(a/b)D′ if (I′)^a⊂I^b for some positive integers a,b. Strict dynamics requires p2*D+≤s p1*D+ and p1*D−≤s p2*D− for some rational 0<s<1. Compact dynamics replaces these by inclusions in the interiors of the right-hand closed subsets in the solid/discrete-adic locale. D+ and D− may intersect. Transposition swaps p1,p2 and D+,D−.
hypotheses: Work with separated finite-type schemes over a noetherian affine base S of finite type over ℤ, and proper compactifications of the correspondence C→X×_S X. All schemes in the solid formalism are of finite type over ℤ; in the Artinian case take A=ℤ_p/p^s or a finite flat coefficient extension.
The coefficient is coherent, with a cohomological correspondence p2*F→p1!F. Limits, colimits and tensor products here are derived solid operations, not exchanges of ordinary module limits.

nodes.title: Siegel degree strata and support pairs
nodes.statement: For n≥1, on the normalization model at Iwahori level p^n, use the self-dual chain A_g→⋯→A_2g→A_1→⋯→A_g and its graded order-p^n groups Gr_i. The degree divisors D_i satisfy D_i+D_(2g+1−i)=V(p^n). Set Z_i=Σ_(j=1)^i D_(g+j), blow up to separate positive and negative parts of Z_i−V(p^(nj)) for every 0≤j≤i, and let the w-stratum be the open on which Gr_(w⁻¹(i)) is multiplicative for i=g+1,…,2g. The closed degree filtration F_r=⋃_(ℓ(w)≤r) Z_>w−1 and D_w,+=⋃_i Z_i,<w_i, D_w,−=⋃_i Z_i,>w_i supply the support pairs. Here w_i counts the multiplicative increments among the first i groups Gr_(g+j). These distinguished strata need not exhaust the ordinary locus for n>1.

Use polarized ordinary Igusa quotients at the cofinal admissible P-levels, with coefficient lattices and their normalized Hecke correspondences specified. For p=2 use the source cofinal subgroup construction rather than an automatic Levi splitting.

nodes.title: Abelian-type descent of analytic coefficients
nodes.statement: Choose a Hodge-type datum (G₁,X₁) and the auxiliary datum B₁=G₁×_(G₁^ab)T of PerfectoidShimuraVarieties §6.4, with compatible neat levels and a cone decomposition refined so that the toroidal compactifications for G₁, B₁ and G are smooth, the one for G₁ is perfect, and the neutral toroidal map f:S^tor,0(B₁)_(K′,Σ)→S^tor,0(G)_(K,Σ) is finite and generically finite étale with group Δ=Δ(K,K′). Let ν_A:Tʳ(Z_p)→A^× be n-analytic, K_p⊆K_(p,m′,0) with m′>n, and ν′_A the induced character for B₁. (1) On the neutral components of the depth-n tube preimages f restricts to a finite map; the Bruhat reduction M_dR,n,K_p for G is the Δ-quotient of the pushout of the B₁ reduction, and the B₁ reduction is the fibre product of the G₁ reduction with the trivial reduction on the zero-dimensional T-Shimura variety; consequently V^n-an_(ν_A)=(f_*V^n-an_(ν′_A))^Δ, and likewise for D^n-an and the −D twists, as sheaves, without asserting compatibility with Hecke actions at level B₁. (2) Every point of the G tube preimage has an affinoid neighbourhood U whose preimage at G₁-level is a Δ-stable union of pregood affinoids, and on such U the sections of V^n-an_(ν_A)(−εD) and D^n-an_(ν_A)(−εD) are projective Banach O(U)⊗̂A-modules. (3) For such U, RΓ(U,V^n-an_(ν_A)(−εD)) is the Δ-invariant direct factor of the corresponding B₁ complex, which is computed from the G₁ complex in the same way. For a Hodge-type datum take G₁=G and Δ trivial: the statement is the supplier's finite-flat trivialization.

Combined with the sheaf-level comparison, H^i(X_Kli(p),Ω(k,r))→H^i(†,k,r) is an isomorphism on slopes <min(k+2r−3,k−2), and on H^0 an isomorphism and on H^1 an injection on slopes <min(k+2r−3,k+1), with cuspidal variants.
